question: A company stores thousands of scanned contracts as PDF files. You need to make the content of those contracts searchable and to surface the key phrases and organisations mentioned in them.
Which type of AI workload does this describe?
explanation: Knowledge mining turns a large volume of unstructured documents into a searchable index.
Azure AI Search runs the documents through an indexer and an optional AI skillset that extracts key phrases and entities, then writes the result into the index.
Anomaly detection looks for outliers, conversational AI holds a dialogue, and computer vision analyses images.

question: Match each scenario to the AI workload that best describes it.
Each workload may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

subs.prompt: Monitor credit card transactions and flag payments that do not fit the usual spending pattern.
Automatically generate a caption that describes the content of a photograph.
Answer employee HR questions through a chat window in Microsoft Teams.

explanation: Anomaly detection compares each new data point against the normal pattern and reports the outliers.
Computer vision works on images and video, so describing a photograph belongs to it.
Conversational AI is a two-way dialogue with a person, which is what a Teams chat bot does.

question: You need to analyse thousands of customer emails and decide whether each message expresses a positive or a negative opinion.
Which type of AI workload does this describe?
explanation: The input is written human language, so this is a natural language processing workload.
Judging whether text is positive or negative is sentiment analysis, a feature of Azure AI Language.

question: Which two scenarios are examples of a natural language processing workload? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.t: Grouping customers into segments based on purchase history
Transcribing a recorded meeting into a written document
Detecting defective parts on a production line from photographs
Extracting the main talking points from a news article
Predicting next month’s electricity demand from historical usage

explanation: Speech-to-text transcription and key phrase extraction both operate on human language, so both are NLP workloads.
Inspecting photographs is computer vision, forecasting a number is regression, and grouping unlabelled customers is clustering.

question: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: Translating a webpage from English into Vietnamese is a natural language processing workload.
Reading the licence plate number from a photograph of a car is a natural language processing workload.
Generating a spoken audio version of a written article is a natural language processing workload.

explanation: Translation and text-to-speech both work on human language, so both are NLP workloads.
Reading a licence plate starts from an image, which makes it optical character recognition — a computer vision workload — even though the output happens to be text.

question: Monitoring the temperature readings of a factory sensor and raising an alert when a reading falls far outside the normal range is an example of anomaly detection.
explanation: Anomaly detection compares incoming values against the pattern learned from historical data and flags the ones that do not fit.
A sensor reading far outside the usual range is exactly such an outlier.

question: A bank wants to identify credit card transactions that differ significantly from a cardholder’s normal behaviour so that possible fraud can be investigated.
Which type of AI workload should the bank use?
explanation: Spotting values that break the established pattern is the definition of anomaly detection.
Watch the wording: the question asks for transactions that are unusual, not for a category to be predicted, so this is not classification.

question: You plan to use Azure AI Language, Azure AI Vision and Azure AI Speech in the same application. You want to manage all three with a single key and endpoint, and to see a single consolidated bill.
Which type of resource should you create?

options.t: A multi-service Azure AI services resource
A separate single-service resource for each service

explanation: A multi-service Azure AI services resource exposes one key and one endpoint that several services share, and it bills them together.
Single-service resources are the right choice only when you want each service billed and managed separately.

question: A hospital trains a model on patient records. The records are encrypted both at rest and in transit, and only authorised clinicians are allowed to read them.
Which Microsoft responsible AI principle does this describe?
explanation: Privacy and security covers protecting the personal data that a model is trained on and operates over.
Encryption, access control and anonymisation are the classic trigger words for this principle.

question: Removing personally identifiable information from a dataset before the model is trained supports the privacy and security principle of responsible AI.
explanation: Anonymising or removing personal data limits what the model and its operators can expose, which is exactly what privacy and security asks for.

question: Which two measures support the privacy and security principle of responsible AI? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.t: Publish the confusion matrix of the model on a public website
Apply role-based access control so that only approved users can read personal data
Add more training images so that the model becomes more accurate
Provide an audio version of the output for users who cannot see the screen
Encrypt the dataset that is used to train the model

explanation: Encryption and role-based access control both restrict who can reach personal data, which is the heart of privacy and security.
Improving accuracy relates to reliability, and providing an audio alternative relates to inclusiveness.

question: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: The privacy and security principle applies only while a model is being trained, not after it is deployed.
Storing training data in an encrypted datastore supports privacy and security.
Anonymising customer names before the data is analysed supports privacy and security.

explanation: Privacy and security applies across the whole lifecycle: collecting, training, deploying and operating the model.
Anonymisation and encryption are both concrete ways to honour the principle.

question: An insurance company sets up a governance board that reviews and signs off every AI model before it goes live, and that remains answerable for the decisions the models make.
Which Microsoft responsible AI principle does this describe?
explanation: Accountability says that people, not models, carry the final responsibility for an AI system.
It shows up as governance structures: review boards, sign-off processes, legal compliance and internal standards.

question: The accountability principle means that the AI system itself, rather than the people who design and operate it, is responsible for its decisions.
explanation: It is the other way round. Accountability puts the responsibility on the people and the organisation that build, deploy and operate the system.

question: A recruitment model consistently scores male applicants higher than equally qualified female applicants.
Which Microsoft responsible AI principle has been violated?
explanation: Fairness requires that an AI system treats all groups of people equally and does not inherit bias from its training data.
A model that favours one gender over another with the same qualifications is the textbook example of unfairness.

question: Which two actions help reduce unfairness in a machine learning model? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.t: Compare the accuracy of the model separately for each demographic group
Increase the number of training epochs
Deploy the model to an Azure Kubernetes Service cluster
Encrypt the model file before it is published
Check whether the training data over-represents one group of people

explanation: Unfairness usually comes from skewed training data, so inspecting the balance of the dataset is the first step.
Measuring performance per group reveals whether the model works worse for some people than for others.
Epochs, deployment targets and encryption have nothing to do with fairness.

question: Match each requirement to the Microsoft responsible AI principle that it belongs to.
Each principle may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

subs.prompt: The system must not favour one group of people over another.
The system must keep working correctly when it meets unusual or missing values.
Users must be able to understand the factors that led to a decision.

explanation: Fairness is about equal treatment across groups of people.
Reliability and safety is about consistent, safe behaviour, including with unusual or missing values.
Transparency is about being able to explain how the system reached its output.

question: Which statement best describes deep learning?

options.t: It selects the best columns of a dataset by hand before training
It stores documents in a search index so that they can be queried
It uses neural networks with many layers that learn features directly from raw data
It groups unlabelled records into clusters of similar items

explanation: Deep learning is a branch of machine learning built on artificial neural networks with many hidden layers.
The layers learn their own representations of the data, so the features do not have to be engineered by hand.
It is especially strong on images, audio and text, but it needs a lot of data and usually a GPU.

question: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: Deep learning always needs less training data than classical machine learning.
Deep learning is a subset of machine learning.
Deep learning models are built from artificial neural networks that contain multiple layers.

explanation: Deep learning sits inside machine learning, which in turn sits inside artificial intelligence.
Its defining feature is the multi-layer neural network.
Deep learning normally needs MORE data, not less, because the network has far more parameters to fit.

question: You are training a deep learning model on a very large set of images and the training job takes days on a standard CPU cluster.
What should you use to shorten the training time?

options.t: A compute instance with a smaller virtual machine size

explanation: Deep learning is dominated by matrix operations, which GPUs execute far faster than CPUs.
An inference cluster serves predictions from a model that is already trained, so it does not help with training.

question: In a deep learning model, the features are engineered manually before training because the network cannot learn them by itself.
explanation: The opposite is true. The hidden layers of a deep neural network learn their own feature representations from the raw input.
That is exactly why deep learning is preferred for images, audio and text, where hand-crafted features are hard to design.

question: Which architecture do modern large language models such as GPT and BERT are built on?
explanation: The Transformer architecture is the foundation of today’s large language models.
K-Means is a clustering algorithm, linear regression is a classical numeric predictor, and a confusion matrix is an evaluation tool, not an architecture.

question: Which mechanism allows a Transformer model to weigh the relationship between every word in a sentence at the same time, instead of reading the words strictly one after another?
explanation: Attention is the core idea of the Transformer: each token can attend to every other token, so long-range context is preserved.
Normalisation rescales numeric columns, cross-validation is an evaluation technique, and bounding boxes belong to object detection.

question: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: Before a Transformer processes text, the text is broken into tokens.
A Transformer must process the words of a sentence strictly from left to right.
The Transformer architecture underpins generative AI language models.

explanation: Transformers are the basis of generative language models, and they work on tokens rather than raw characters or whole words.
Unlike recurrent networks, a Transformer looks at all positions in parallel through attention, so it is not restricted to left-to-right reading.

question: In a Transformer-based language model, what is an embedding?

options.t: The rectangle that surrounds a detected object in an image
The percentage of predictions that the model got right
The compute target on which the model is deployed
A numeric vector that represents the meaning of a token

explanation: An embedding maps a token to a vector of numbers, positioning items with similar meaning close together in the vector space.
Embeddings are what make semantic search and retrieval augmented generation possible.

question: A data scientist needs a personal, always-available development environment in Azure Machine Learning studio for writing and testing notebooks.
Which compute resource should the data scientist use?
explanation: A compute instance is a single managed virtual machine intended as a personal workstation for authoring and running notebooks.
A compute cluster scales out for training jobs, and an inference cluster serves deployed models.

question: Match each requirement to the Azure Machine Learning compute resource that fits it best.
Each resource may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

subs.prompt: Run a training job that scales out across several nodes and shuts the nodes down when the job finishes.
Serve real-time predictions from a deployed model in production.
Give one data scientist a managed virtual machine for interactive notebook work.

explanation: Compute clusters are elastic: they add nodes for a training job and scale back to zero afterwards, so you only pay while training.
Inference clusters, backed by Azure Kubernetes Service, host real-time endpoints in production.
Compute instances are single-user development boxes.

question: In an Azure Machine Learning workspace, which object stores the connection information to an Azure Storage account so that the same data source can be reused without repeating the credentials?
explanation: A datastore keeps the connection details for a data source, such as an Azure Storage account, inside the workspace.
Datasets are then defined on top of a datastore so that experiments can reference the data by name.

question: A compute cluster in Azure Machine Learning can automatically scale the number of nodes up and down based on the workload.
explanation: A compute cluster is defined with a minimum and a maximum node count and scales between them as jobs arrive and finish.
Setting the minimum to zero means you pay nothing while the cluster is idle.

question: Match each scenario to the machine learning technique that it uses.
Each technique may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

subs.prompt: Estimate how many litres of milk a shop will sell tomorrow.
Decide whether an incoming email is spam or not spam.
Group news articles that talk about similar topics, without any labels being supplied.

explanation: Predicting a number is regression, predicting a known label is classification, and grouping unlabelled data is clustering.
Regression and classification are supervised; clustering is unsupervised.

question: Which machine learning technique does NOT require labelled training data?
explanation: Clustering is unsupervised: it discovers the groups itself, so no labels are supplied.
Regression and both flavours of classification are supervised techniques and need labelled examples.

question: A binary classification model has an AUC of 0.42.
What does that tell you about the model?

options.t: It performs worse than random guessing
It performs slightly better than random guessing
AUC cannot be used for classification models

explanation: An AUC of 0.5 is the score you would get by guessing at random.
Anything below 0.5 therefore means the model is doing worse than a coin toss; 1.0 would be a perfect classifier.

question: Match each evaluation metric to the type of model it is normally reported for.
Each model type may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

subs.prompt: Coefficient of determination (R squared)
Precision and recall
Root mean squared error (RMSE)

explanation: Regression predicts numbers, so it is scored on how far the predictions are from the true values: R squared and RMSE.
Classification predicts labels, so it is scored from the confusion matrix: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and AUC.

question: A mobile app takes a photograph of a single piece of fruit and reports whether it is an apple, a banana or an orange. The app does not need to know where in the picture the fruit is.
Which computer vision solution does this describe?
explanation: Image classification assigns one label to the whole image together with a confidence score, and says nothing about position.
Object detection would also return a bounding box, which the app does not need.

question: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: An image classification model returns a confidence score between 0 and 1 alongside the predicted label.
An image classification model returns the coordinates of each object it recognises.
Adding more training images is a valid way to improve a weak image classification model.

explanation: Classification returns a label plus a confidence value, but no coordinates — coordinates come from object detection.
When a classification model performs poorly, the standard first remedy is to supply more, and more varied, training images.

question: You need to extract the text of a 200-page scanned PDF document so that it can be indexed.
Which Azure AI Vision capability should you use?
explanation: The Read API is designed for text-heavy and multi-page documents, including PDFs, and runs asynchronously.
The older OCR API is aimed at small amounts of text in a single image.

question: Optical character recognition can extract handwritten text as well as printed text from an image.
explanation: Azure AI Vision OCR reads both printed and handwritten text, which is why it is used for forms, notes and cheques as well as documents.

question: You need to identify famous buildings and monuments in tourist photographs without training a model of your own.
Which Azure AI Vision feature should you use?

options.t: Categories with the landmarks domain model

explanation: Azure AI Vision ships domain-specific models; the landmarks domain recognises well-known places, and the celebrities domain recognises well-known people.
Custom Vision would require you to gather and label your own training images.

question: A retailer wants to train a model that recognises its own product packaging, using photographs taken in its own stores.
Which service should the retailer use?
explanation: Custom Vision is the service for training a vision model on your own labelled images.
Azure AI Vision image analysis is pre-built and cannot be taught new, company-specific classes.

question: A car park system must count how many vehicles are in a photograph and report where each one is.
Which computer vision solution should be used?
explanation: Object detection returns a class label, a probability and a bounding box for every object it finds, so it can both count and locate the vehicles.
Image classification would only say that the photograph contains cars, without counting or locating them.

question: Which two conditions are most likely to reduce the accuracy of a facial detection solution? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.t: Photographs taken with a colour camera
Subjects standing directly in front of the camera
Images stored in an encrypted datastore

explanation: Face detection degrades when the face is partly hidden, badly lit or seen from an extreme angle.
Colour photographs, frontal poses and encryption of the stored images have no negative effect on detection accuracy.

question: You need to scan support tickets and pull out the names of people, the companies they work for and the dates they mention.
Which Azure AI Language feature should you use?
explanation: Named entity recognition finds and categorises entities such as people, organisations, locations, dates and quantities in text.
Sentiment analysis measures tone, language detection identifies the language, and summarisation shortens the text.

question: A company must find and redact national identity numbers, phone numbers and email addresses in customer chat transcripts before the transcripts are archived.
Which Azure AI Language capability should the company use?
explanation: PII detection is the variant of entity recognition that finds personal identifiers so that they can be masked or removed.
It is the feature to reach for whenever a question mentions redacting or protecting personal data in text.

question: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: Entity recognition can categorise a detected entity as a person, a location or an organisation.
Entity linking connects a recognised entity to an entry in a knowledge source such as Wikipedia.
Entity recognition returns an overall positive or negative score for the document.

explanation: Entity recognition categorises entities and, through entity linking, can resolve them to a well-known reference.
An overall positive or negative score is what sentiment analysis produces, not entity recognition.

question: Match each requirement to the Azure AI Language feature that meets it.
Each feature may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

subs.prompt: List the organisations and dates mentioned in a contract.
Decide whether a hotel review is complimentary or critical.
Determine which language an incoming message was written in.

explanation: Entity recognition extracts things, sentiment analysis measures feeling, and language detection identifies the language.
All three are features of the single Azure AI Language service.

question: A virtual assistant must work out what a user wants when they type “book me a flight to Da Nang next Friday”, and extract the destination and the date.
Which Azure AI Language capability should you use?
explanation: Conversational Language Understanding predicts the intent behind an utterance and extracts the entities it contains.
Question answering only looks up a stored answer for a question; it does not infer intent or extract parameters.

question: Match each example to the Conversational Language Understanding element that it represents.
Each element may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

subs.prompt: “Turn off the lights in the kitchen” typed by a user
TurnOffDevice
kitchen

explanation: An utterance is what the user actually said or typed.
An intent is the action the user wants performed.
An entity is a detail inside the utterance that the intent needs, such as the room name.

question: For each of the following statements about Conversational Language Understanding, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: Conversational Language Understanding can determine the intent of a user utterance.
Conversational Language Understanding replaces the need for a knowledge base when answering frequently asked questions.
A model is trained from example utterances that you label with intents and entities.

explanation: You author intents and entities, then supply labelled example utterances and train the model.
For frequently asked questions the right tool is question answering with a knowledge base; the two features are often used side by side in one bot.

question: In a Conversational Language Understanding model, what is an utterance?

options.t: The action that the user wants the application to perform
A numeric score between 0 and 1 for the tone of the text
A rectangle drawn around an object in an image
An example of something a user might say or type

explanation: Utterances are the sample phrases you provide so that the model learns how real users express each intent.
The action itself is the intent; the tone score belongs to sentiment analysis and the rectangle to object detection.

question: A podcast publisher needs written transcripts of hundreds of recorded episodes.
Which Azure AI Speech capability should the publisher use?
explanation: Speech to text converts recorded or live audio into written text and can run in batch mode over many files.
Text to speech goes the other way, turning written text into spoken audio.

question: A news website wants blind visitors to be able to listen to its articles read out in a natural voice.
Which Azure AI Speech capability meets this requirement?
explanation: Text to speech synthesises spoken audio from written text.
Note that this scenario also illustrates the inclusiveness principle of responsible AI.

question: During an international conference, spoken English must be turned into spoken Vietnamese in near real time.
Which capability should be used?
explanation: Speech translation takes spoken input in one language and produces the translation, which can then be spoken aloud.
Text translation only handles written text, so it does not cover the audio input on its own.

question: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: Speech to text can process audio in real time as well as in batch.
Text to speech is used to create an audio version of a written document.
Speech to text requires you to train your own language model before it can be used.

explanation: Speech to text works both in real time and in batch, and text to speech produces spoken audio from text.
Out of the box, speech to text uses the Universal Language Model trained by Microsoft; custom models are optional, for specialist vocabulary.

question: Match each scenario to the speech capability that fits it.
Each capability may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

subs.prompt: Produce a written record of a customer support call.
Announce train departures aloud from a text timetable.
Let a French speaker and a Japanese speaker talk to each other by phone.

explanation: Audio in and text out is speech to text; text in and audio out is text to speech.
When both the input and the output are speech but the language changes, it is speech translation.

question: Which three capabilities are provided by the Azure AI Language service? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.t: Model training with the Azure Machine Learning designer

explanation: Azure AI Language is the unified text service: sentiment analysis, key phrase extraction, named entity recognition, language detection, summarisation, question answering and conversational language understanding.
Object detection belongs to computer vision, and the designer belongs to Azure Machine Learning.

question: You need to shorten long product manuals into a few sentences that capture their main content.
Which Azure AI Language feature should you use?
explanation: Summarisation produces a condensed version of a document while keeping the essential information.
Do not confuse it with key phrase extraction, which returns a list of phrases rather than readable prose.

question: Question answering and conversational language understanding are both features of the Azure AI Language service.
explanation: Azure AI Language brought the former QnA Maker and LUIS capabilities together into one service.
They are frequently combined in a single bot: question answering handles the FAQ, conversational language understanding handles the commands.

question: Which Azure resource lets a single application use Azure AI Language, Azure AI Vision and Azure AI Speech through one endpoint and one key?

options.t: An Azure AI services multi-service resource

explanation: The multi-service Azure AI services resource shares one endpoint and one key across the services it covers.
A Language resource covers only the Language service.

question: Which three capabilities are part of the Azure AI Speech service? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
explanation: Azure AI Speech covers speech to text, text to speech, speech translation and speaker recognition.
Image tagging belongs to Azure AI Vision, and clustering is a machine learning technique.

question: Which model does Azure AI Speech use by default for speech to text, before any customisation is applied?

options.t: The Universal Language Model trained by Microsoft
A model that you must train from your own recordings

explanation: Out of the box, speech to text uses a Universal Language Model trained with Microsoft-owned data that reflects commonly used spoken language.
Custom speech models are optional and are used for specialist vocabulary or unusual acoustic conditions.

question: Speaker recognition, which identifies who is talking, is a capability of the Azure AI Speech service.
explanation: Speaker recognition sits in Azure AI Speech alongside speech to text, text to speech and speech translation.
It answers “who spoke” rather than “what was said”.

question: A publisher wants an automatic list of the main talking points of each article so that editors can scan them quickly.
Which Azure AI Language feature should be used?
explanation: Key phrase extraction returns the main talking points of a piece of text.
The phrase “main talking points” in a question is a reliable signal for this feature.

question: Key phrase extraction returns a numeric score that indicates whether the text is positive or negative.
explanation: Key phrase extraction returns a list of the main phrases in the text, not a sentiment score.
The positive or negative score is produced by sentiment analysis.

question: A sentiment analysis call returns a score of 0.94 for a customer review.
How should the review be interpreted?

options.t: As a review written in an undetermined language

explanation: Sentiment scores run from 0 to 1: values close to 1 are positive, values close to 0 are negative and values around 0.5 are neutral.
A score of 0.94 is therefore clearly positive.

question: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: Sentiment analysis can be used to decide whether social media posts about a brand are favourable.
A sentiment score close to 0.5 indicates neutral or indeterminate sentiment.
Sentiment analysis identifies which language a document is written in.

explanation: Sentiment analysis measures tone, which is exactly what brand monitoring needs, and scores near 0.5 mean the tone is unclear.
Identifying the language of a document is language detection.

question: A company must publish the same written press release in twelve languages at once.
Which Azure service should the company use?
explanation: Azure AI Translator translates written text and can return several target languages from a single request.
Speech-to-text would be the answer only if the source material were audio.

question: Match each requirement to the service that meets it.
Each service may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

subs.prompt: Translate the written text of a website into Spanish.
Translate a live spoken presentation into another language.
Read the printed text on a photograph of a street sign.

explanation: Written text goes to Azure AI Translator, spoken language goes to Azure AI Speech, and text inside an image goes to Azure AI Vision OCR.
Always look at the input format first: text, audio or image.

question: Which statement best describes what a large language model (LLM) does?

options.t: It generates new content in response to a prompt
It groups unlabelled records into clusters
It draws bounding boxes around objects in an image
It measures how far a numeric prediction is from the true value

explanation: A large language model is a generative model: given a prompt, it produces new text that continues or answers it.
Clustering, object detection and error measurement are all tasks of other kinds of model.

question: Before a language model processes a piece of text, the text is split into smaller units that the model works with.
What are those units called?
explanation: Text is broken into tokens, which may be whole words or parts of words, and the model reads and generates one token at a time.
Pricing and context limits for language models are also expressed in tokens.

question: Match each task to the type of model that performs it.
Each model may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

subs.prompt: Create an illustration from a written description.
options: An image generation model such as DALL·E
A speech recognition model such as Whisper
A text generation model such as GPT

subs.prompt: Transcribe an audio recording into text.
options: An image generation model such as DALL·E
A speech recognition model such as Whisper
A text generation model such as GPT

subs.prompt: Draft a summary of a long report.
options: An image generation model such as DALL·E
A speech recognition model such as Whisper
A text generation model such as GPT

explanation: Azure OpenAI offers several model families: GPT models for text, DALL·E for images, Whisper for speech recognition and embedding models for vector representations.
Match the model family to the kind of content that has to be produced or understood.

question: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: Generative AI models are built on the Transformer architecture.
An embedding represents the meaning of text as a vector of numbers.
A large language model stores an exact copy of every document it was trained on and looks the answer up.

explanation: Generative language models are Transformer based and use embeddings to represent meaning numerically.
A language model does not store or look up its training documents; it generates the next token from learned statistical patterns, which is why it can produce plausible but wrong answers.

question: Which type of model is used to convert text into vectors so that items with similar meaning are placed close together?
explanation: Embedding models turn text into numeric vectors that capture semantic similarity.
They are the foundation of vector search and of retrieval augmented generation.

question: Which three tasks are typical uses of generative AI? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.t: Detecting an unusual spike in server CPU usage
Splitting a dataset into training and validation rows
Drafting a marketing email from a short brief
Suggesting code to a developer inside an editor

explanation: Generative AI creates new content: drafts, summaries, translations, code and images.
Spotting an unusual spike is anomaly detection, and splitting a dataset is a step of the classic machine learning workflow.

question: What is the main difference between generative AI and traditional machine learning such as classification?

options.t: Generative AI can only work with images
Generative AI always runs on a compute instance
Generative AI creates new content, whereas classification assigns an existing label
Generative AI never needs any training data

explanation: Traditional models predict a value or a category that already exists in the label set.
Generative models produce new content — text, code or images — that was not in the training set verbatim.

question: A software company wants an assistant that is embedded in its product, understands the user’s current context and helps them complete tasks in natural language.
What is this kind of application usually called?
explanation: A copilot is a generative AI assistant built into an application to help users get work done in natural language.
Indexers, compute clusters and confusion matrices belong to search, training infrastructure and evaluation respectively.

question: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: Predicting tomorrow’s temperature from historical weather data is a generative AI scenario.
Generating product descriptions from a list of attributes is a generative AI scenario.
Answering employee questions over internal company documents is a generative AI scenario.

explanation: Writing descriptions and answering questions over your own documents both produce new language, so both are generative AI.
Forecasting a number from historical data is regression, a traditional machine learning task.

question: Which scenario is NOT a use of generative AI?

options.t: Writing a first draft of a job advertisement
Translating a document into another language
Generating an image from a text description
Grouping customers into segments based on purchase history

explanation: Grouping customers without labels is clustering, a traditional unsupervised machine learning technique.
Drafting text, translating and generating images all create new content, so they are generative AI.

question: You want a language model to answer questions using your company’s own product documentation, which the model was never trained on.
Which technique should you use?
explanation: RAG retrieves the relevant passages from your own data and puts them into the prompt, so the model answers from that grounded context.
It is the standard answer whenever a question mentions answering over private or company-specific documents.

question: In a chat completion request, what is the purpose of the system message?

options.t: To measure the accuracy of the generated answer
To set the role, tone and rules that the model should follow
To store the user’s password for the session
To choose the compute cluster that will run the model

explanation: The system message tells the model who it is meant to be and what constraints apply, before any user message is processed.
It is the first and cheapest lever in prompt engineering.

question: A prompt includes two worked examples of the input and the expected output before the real question is asked.
What is this technique called?
explanation: Providing a small number of examples inside the prompt is few-shot prompting; providing none is zero-shot.
Examples show the model the format and style you expect, which usually improves the answer without any retraining.

question: What does grounding a generative AI model mean?

options.t: Reducing the size of the model so it runs on a phone
Encrypting the model weights before deployment
Splitting the dataset into training and validation rows
Supplying trusted, relevant data in the context so the answer is based on it

explanation: Grounding means anchoring the model’s answer in data you trust, usually by placing that data in the prompt context.
A grounded answer is far less likely to be a hallucination, and it can cite where the information came from.

question: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: Retrieval Augmented Generation changes the weights of the underlying model.
Rewriting a vague prompt to be more specific usually improves the quality of the response.
Retrieval Augmented Generation adds relevant data to the prompt at query time.

explanation: Clearer prompts produce better answers, and RAG works purely at query time by injecting retrieved context.
Changing the weights of the model is fine-tuning, which is a different and much more expensive technique.

question: Match each description to the prompt engineering technique it refers to.
Each technique may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

subs.prompt: Tell the model “You are a helpful travel agent who answers in Vietnamese.”
Show the model three sample questions with their ideal answers.
Search the company knowledge base and paste the matching passages into the prompt.

explanation: A system message sets the persona and rules, few-shot examples demonstrate the expected output, and RAG injects retrieved facts.
The three techniques are complementary and are often used together.

question: A language model produces an answer that sounds convincing but contains facts that are simply untrue.
What is this behaviour called?
explanation: A hallucination is generated content that is fluent and plausible but factually wrong.
Grounding the model on trusted data and keeping a human reviewer in the loop are the usual mitigations.

question: Which Azure service is designed to detect and block harmful content such as hate, violence, self-harm and sexual material in both text and images?
explanation: Azure AI Content Safety scores content across harm categories and can block it before it reaches a user.
It is used on both the prompt going in and the completion coming out.

question: Which three practices reduce the risks of a generative AI application? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.t: Apply content filters to prompts and responses
Keep a human reviewer in the loop for high-impact decisions
Publish the model endpoint without any authentication
Remove all logging so that nothing is recorded
Ground the model on trusted, approved data sources

explanation: Grounding, content filtering and human oversight are the standard mitigations for hallucination, harmful output and misuse.
Removing authentication and logging makes an application less safe, not more.

question: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: Because a generative model is trained on public data, its output never needs to be reviewed.
Transparency for a generative AI application includes telling users that they are interacting with AI.
Prompt injection is an attack in which crafted input makes the model ignore its original instructions.

explanation: Prompt injection tries to override the system message with instructions hidden in the user input or in retrieved content.
Generated output always needs review, and disclosing that a user is talking to an AI system is a core transparency requirement.

question: A bank plans to use a generative AI model to draft replies to customer complaints. Which safeguard best addresses the risk of an inaccurate or inappropriate reply reaching a customer?

options.t: Require a staff member to review and approve each reply before it is sent
Increase the maximum number of tokens in the response
Deploy the model to a larger virtual machine
Turn off logging for the endpoint

explanation: Human review before the content reaches the customer is the direct mitigation for inaccurate or inappropriate generated text.
Token limits and virtual machine size affect length and performance, not correctness, and removing logging weakens accountability.

question: Which Azure platform brings together model discovery, a playground for experimentation, and tools to build, evaluate and deploy generative AI solutions?
explanation: Azure AI Foundry is the unified platform for the whole generative AI lifecycle: explore models, prototype in the playground, evaluate, then deploy.
Work is organised into projects and hubs.

question: In Azure AI Foundry, what is the playground used for?

options.t: Creating a search index from a data source
Scaling a compute cluster up and down
Trying prompts against a model interactively before writing any code
Labelling images for an object detection model

explanation: The playground is an interactive workspace for experimenting with prompts, system messages and model parameters.
It is the fastest way to see how a model behaves before you build an application around it.

question: For each of the following statements about Azure AI Foundry, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

subs.prompt: Azure AI Foundry can only be used with models that you have trained yourself.
Azure AI Foundry lets you compare and deploy models from more than one provider.
Azure AI Foundry includes tooling to evaluate the quality and safety of a generative AI application.

explanation: Foundry exposes a catalog of models from Microsoft, OpenAI and other providers, plus evaluation and content-safety tooling.
Training your own model is not a prerequisite — most projects start from a pre-built model in the catalog.

question: In Azure AI Foundry, how is related work such as models, data connections and deployments usually organised?
explanation: A Foundry project groups the assets for one solution: model deployments, connected data, evaluations and configuration.
Projects can share resources through a hub.

question: A company wants to use GPT models but requires enterprise security, private networking and Azure role-based access control.
Which service should the company use?
explanation: Azure OpenAI Service delivers the OpenAI models on Azure infrastructure with enterprise security, private networking and access management.
It is the answer whenever a question pairs OpenAI models with Azure governance requirements.

question: Which three model families are available through Azure OpenAI Service? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.t: Indexer models for building search indexes

explanation: Azure OpenAI hosts GPT for text, DALL·E for images, Whisper for speech recognition and embedding models for vectors.
K-Means is a classical clustering algorithm, and an indexer is a component of Azure AI Search, not a model family.

question: Content filtering is applied to Azure OpenAI Service deployments to help block harmful prompts and responses.
explanation: Azure OpenAI applies content filters to both the input prompt and the generated completion, across harm categories such as hate, violence, self-harm and sexual content.
This is part of Microsoft’s responsible AI commitments for the service.

question: Before an application can send requests to a GPT model in Azure OpenAI Service, what must be created first?
explanation: You deploy a chosen model into your Azure OpenAI resource; the deployment name is then used in every API request.
Skillsets belong to Azure AI Search, and confusion matrices and bounding boxes belong to evaluation and computer vision.

question: What is the Azure AI Foundry model catalog?

options.t: A list of the datasets stored in a workspace
A record of every prediction that a deployed model has made
A set of rules that filter harmful content
A library of models from several providers that can be compared and deployed

explanation: The model catalog gathers models from Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta, Mistral and others in one place.
You can compare them on capability, cost and benchmarks, then deploy the one you pick straight from the catalog.

question: Which two criteria are commonly used to choose a model from the Azure AI Foundry model catalog? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.t: The number of rows in the training dataset of your own application
The name of the resource group
The task the model is designed for, such as chat or embeddings
The cost of running the model
The colour scheme of the Azure portal

explanation: Models are compared on what they can do, how well they score on benchmarks, and how much they cost to run.
Portal theming, resource group names and your own dataset size are not selection criteria for a catalog model.

question: The Azure AI Foundry model catalog contains models from Microsoft and from third-party providers such as OpenAI, Meta and Mistral.
explanation: The catalog is deliberately multi-provider so that you can pick the model that best fits the task, the budget and the compliance requirements.
